text:
Alexa: Quick design review: proposing we split the Private setup wizard into a lightweight 'connectivity quick-check' early in the flow, then the full agent/credentials steps later. Current order surprises users — they hit the SSH key + agent steps then fail network checks and blame the console.

Mike: +1. If we run lightweight checks earlier we can surface provider-specific hints (GCP firewall tag, AWS SG rule examples) right away. Means fewer support tickets. :raised_hands:

Sam: Heads-up: moving checks earlier affects the permissions we ask for up-front. Right now the full preflight runs with the agent and collected logs. We can do a read-only, zero-credentials probe first (DNS resolve, TCP connect). Need to confirm perf impact.

Devon: Product note: split seems lower risk if the early step is explicit about "no credentials, quick probes only". Suggested copy: 

Step title: Network quick check
Body copy: "Run a lightweight connectivity test to verify DNS and HTTPS reachability. This does not install anything or require credentials. If the quick check fails, we'll show targeted remediation steps."
Primary button: "Run quick check"

Julie: A11y nits: keyboard focus order must follow visual order when we move this step. Make sure the step headings use role="heading" and aria-level set, and that status updates use aria-live="polite". Also the green check icon color contrast is currently ~2.8:1 on our pale green — fails AA. Use a darker green or add a checked-outline for non-color indicators.

Mike: Copy suggestion for failing state (short, action-oriented): 

"Quick check failed — we couldn't reach your endpoint on port 443. Try adding an outbound rule for TCP 443, or run this on your bastion: 

curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://YOUR-ENDPOINT.example.com/health"

Alexa: UX detail: inline diagnostics should let users copy a one-line firewall rule for common clouds. Example: 

AWS SG: `aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-1234 --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0`

Not ideal long-term (security risk) but helpful for quick troubleshooting in demos and proofs-of-concept. Mark the rule as sample only.

Sam: Implementation question — can we run the quick-check purely from the browser (fetch, WebRTC-like)? Browser-based TCP check is limited. We likely need a short-running server-side probe (no credentials) from the control plane or let users run a helper CLI. Either way, surface the difference in the UI.

Devon: Action items: 
- Alexa to iterate copy + low-fi mockups for early quick-check and failing state (due Tue).
- Sam to draft backend feasibility options (browser-safe probe vs control-plane probe vs CLI helper).
- Julie to provide WCAG contrast/pass suggestions and keyboard-flow checklist.

Julie: Also recommend: announcements for screen readers when test starts/completes: aria-live="polite" for progress text and aria-atomic="true" for final result. Use text labels in addition to color: "Passed", "Warning", "Failed".

deploy-bot: deployment:staging 1893456855 - new quick-check UI prototype deployed to staging for review.

Mike: I'll test the staging flow and paste screenshots. Can we also add a small 'why we ask this' tooltip next to the Run button (one-liner) to reduce distrust from security teams?

Alexa: Agreed — tooltip copy: "Performs basic DNS and HTTPS checks from our staging probes. No keys or agents installed." Short, scannable.

Devon: Cool — we'll bring this to the weekly UX sync. Thanks everyone. :tada:
